skill.name: schedule-with-outlook
skill.description: Use Rarefriend MCP to manage Outlook contacts, calendar scheduling, Teams meetings, relationship notes, and tags from an AI assistant.
skill.summary: Search Outlook contacts, find free time, schedule meetings, and manage Rarefriend notes with Microsoft calendar context.
skill.author: Whitefield-Labs

security_audit.summary: The apparent mass of Ruby backtick findings is mostly false positive Markdown markup around tool names and examples. Two external-command findings are confirmed because setup instructs users to run an unpinned third-party MCP package with client credentials. I also found semantic privacy risks around broad Microsoft email scope and third-party handling of Outlook and Rarefriend data.

remediation.suggestion: Pin @rarefriend-ai/mcp to a reviewed version, publish checksums, and explain that npx runs third-party code.

remediation.issue: Plain client secrets in local AI client configuration
remediation.suggestion: Prefer a browser OAuth flow or short-lived tokens, and document secret rotation and local file permissions.
Keep this skill limited to contacts and calendar, or require separate confirmation before connecting Microsoft email.
Require explicit user confirmation before creating, rescheduling, canceling events, or deleting notes.

content.value_statement: Coordinating Outlook meetings often requires switching between contacts, calendars, and notes. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code to use Rarefriend MCP tools for Outlook scheduling and relationship context.
actual_capabilities: Detect whether Rarefriend MCP and Microsoft integrations are connected.
Search Outlook and Rarefriend contacts by name, company, role, email, tag, or source.
Find available Outlook calendar time before creating meetings.
Create, reschedule, and cancel Outlook calendar events through MCP tools.
Create and manage Rarefriend notes and tags for contact relationship context.
Guide users through Microsoft and Rarefriend connection setup.
limitations: Requires a Rarefriend account and the @rarefriend-ai/mcp server.
Requires Microsoft account authorization for each integration.
Microsoft contacts are read-only through the Outlook tools.
Setup uses a third-party MCP package and may store credentials in client configuration.

use_cases.title: Book a Teams Meeting
use_cases.description: Find an Outlook contact, check shared availability, and create a calendar event after user confirmation.

use_cases.title: Prepare for Relationship Follow-Up
use_cases.description: Review contact notes, add meeting context, and keep important relationship details pinned in Rarefriend.

use_cases.title: Organize Outlook Contacts
use_cases.description: Search contacts by company or role, confirm source labels, and apply tags for future outreach.

prompt_templates.title: Check Setup
prompt_templates.prompt: Check whether Rarefriend MCP and my Microsoft calendar are connected. If not, show the setup steps I need.

prompt_templates.title: Find a Contact
prompt_templates.prompt: Find {person} in my Outlook contacts and show their email, company, and source label.

prompt_templates.title: Schedule a Meeting
prompt_templates.prompt: Find a 30 minute time next week with {person}. Confirm the best slot with me before creating the Outlook event.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Follow-Up Workflow
prompt_templates.prompt: Review my recent notes for {account}, find the right contact, identify open times this week, and draft a meeting title and agenda before scheduling.

output_examples.input: Find time with Maya next week.
output_examples.output: I found Maya Patel in Microsoft Contacts. Tuesday at 10:00 AM and Thursday at 2:30 PM are open. Please choose a slot before I create the event.

output_examples.input: What meetings do I have this week?
output_examples.output: Monday: product review at 9:00 AM. Wednesday: customer call at 1:00 PM. Friday: team planning at 3:00 PM.

output_examples.input: Add a note after my call with Jordan.
output_examples.output: I found Jordan Lee and added the note to Rarefriend. I also pinned it because you marked the follow-up as important.

best_practices: Check connected integrations before using calendar or contact tools.
Confirm dates, time zones, attendees, and title before creating or moving events.
Use notes and tags only for relevant relationship context.
anti_patterns: Do not schedule or cancel meetings without explicit user confirmation.
Do not request the email integration when contacts or calendar access is enough.
Do not store real client secrets in prompts, chat history, or shared files.

faq.question: Does this work without Rarefriend?
faq.answer: No. It requires a Rarefriend account and the Rarefriend MCP server.

faq.question: Can it create Teams meetings?
faq.answer: It can create Outlook calendar events with attendees. Teams behavior depends on the Microsoft and Rarefriend integration.

faq.question: Can it edit Outlook contacts?
faq.answer: No. The skill states that Microsoft contacts are read-only through the Outlook tools.

faq.question: Does it access email?
faq.answer: The setup can connect Microsoft email, but scheduling normally needs contacts and calendar only.

faq.question: Which assistants are supported?
faq.answer: The skill declares support for Claude, Codex, and Claude Code.

faq.question: Is setup automatic?
faq.answer: No. The user must install and configure Rarefriend MCP and authorize Microsoft access.
